deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page, so there are no derivations to reconstruct. Folio 65r is a set of reading notes, part paraphrase and part excerpt, from J. F. Herbart's 'Kurze Encyklopädie der Philosophie aus praktischen Gesichtspunkten entworfen' (1831; 2nd ed. 1841). The heading 'Encyklopädie' and the running § numbers 238–245, continued on the next page with §§244–249 and §§203–206, match that book's closing chapter on the method and systematic form of philosophy. The previous page holds Riemann's English excerpts from Locke's Essay II.21 on liberty and the will, so the bundle is a reading notebook.

Content, section by section:

(§238) Logic comes alive where people argue about concepts. It is supplemented by the remarks that arise about the relations and possible combinations of concepts.

(§239) Mathematical versus philosophical inquiry. Doctrines whose development is deductive carry a hypothetical character. There the premise is never itself knowledge; only the judgment is. Metaphysical research rests neither on judgments nor on intuitions but on corrected (reworked) concepts. Practical philosophy has judgments, but not by inference. They are aesthetic judgments about the will: it attaches subjects (pictures of the will) to the predicates 'praiseworthy' and 'blameworthy'. Its essential task is to find the series of relations under which the will must be thought in order to be an object of aesthetic judgment. The concepts of these relations are the law. A crossed-out start notes that this is far from the mathematician's discursive manner of knowing.

(§240) The notes turn from concepts as objects of thought to the seeking and finding of them, and set out three cases:
- Case 1 (§241, 'Vorstellung, Verstand und Vernunft'): explicating concepts long in use whose sense one cannot state.
- Case 2 (§§242–243): fixing concepts in use that for practical reasons must not depend on that usage. A wavering concept is made firm by drawing on the marks of neighbouring concepts that bound it (Wohlwollen – Recht – Billigkeit). The exception is when the fault is a contradiction, as with Neigung/Vorsatz; then only new concepts help.
- Case 3 (§§244–245): generating new concepts where the old ones do not suffice.

(§242, with §241 'Synthese u. Analyse') Herbart's two kinds of systematics: one sets concepts side by side, the other one after another. Synthesis must be completed by analysis, which starts from the old concept as found in language, in contradictory discourse and in experience. This stops synthesis from forcing on words meanings they cannot bear.

Herbart then mocks the advice to begin with analysis, or to drop synthesis altogether. That is the 'proven means' of never moving and staying inside the old circle of opinion. Analysis is not hard; it runs every danger of surreptitious assumption ('Erschleichung'), and each party finds in it what it wants. Synthesis, by contrast, uses calculation, sees what comes out, and so leaves the circle of mere imagination. The analytic type merely repeats its own image and feeds self-deception.

The page is evidence for Riemann's close study of Herbart's methodology, specifically the theme of revising and generating concepts ('Bearbeitung der Begriffe'). That theme is relevant to the conceptual style of the Habilitationsvortrag, but the page contains nothing of Riemann's own.
errors: No mathematical steps, so no mathematical errors. As an excerpt, the text follows Herbart's line of thought; any slips would be copying or paraphrase issues and cannot be judged without collating the 1831/1841 edition.

results.what: Excerpt and paraphrase of Herbart, Kurze Encyklopädie der Philosophie, §§238–245: philosophical versus mathematical inquiry, three cases of seeking and finding concepts, synthesis versus analysis in concept formation
results.modern_name: Herbartian methodology of concept revision ('Bearbeitung der Begriffe'); synthetic/analytic method in philosophy

deep.surprise_reason: These are reading notes copied from Herbart's Encyklopädie, with no mathematics and no original content. Riemann's extensive Herbart excerpts in the Naturphilosophie papers are well documented (e.g. E. Scholz, 'Herbart's influence on Bernhard Riemann', Historia Mathematica 1982).
transcription_corrections: Second heading likely reads 'Über das Wechseln [Wechsel?] in der Philosophie und über die daraus entstehende Form' rather than 'Über das Wahre'; uncertain.
§239, line 2: 'Die Erkenntniss selbst ist hier niemals ein Erkennen' more plausibly reads 'Die Voraussetzung selbst ist hier niemals eine Erkenntniss, sondern nur das Urtheil ist eine solche'.
§239: 'ruhen sich weder auf Urtheile' should be 'stützen sich weder auf Urtheile'. The end of that sentence appears to be '...verbesserte Begriffe als Hauptgegenstände', not 'Hauptgrundlage'.
Crossed-out line: 'Die discursive Erkenntniss und Forschungsweise des Mathematikers [ist] weit entfernt'. It continues the unfinished 'Also auch hier ist...' and is not a separate §240.
§240 case 2: 'gehörig angrenzen würden' is probably 'gehörig begrenzen würden' (neighbouring concepts bound the wavering one).

Last paragraph: 'Jede Partei [-hält-]' is likely followed by 'findet, was sie haben will'. 'die Verbesserung der Selbsttäuschungen' should probably be 'Vermehrung' (or similar) of self-deceptions, since the sense is pejorative toward analysis.
Source identification to add: this is an excerpt from Herbart's Kurze Encyklopädie der Philosophie, not Riemann's own text.
